title: Box 16.01 Revised Care for CMMRD (C4CMMRD) indication criteria for constitutional mismatch repair deficiency syndrome (CMMRD) testing in patients with cancera

C4CMMRD scoring points assigned to (pre)malignancies in the patient (≥ 1 point is mandatory):

·    Carcinoma of LS spectrumb and/or a high-grade dysplastic adenoma of the digestive tract at age < 25 years

3 points

·    Multiple colorectal adenomas at age < 25 years and no genetic diagnosis/explanation upon testing for polyposis syndromes

3 points

·    T-cell lymphoblastic lymphoma at age < 18 years

2 points

·    WHO grade III or IV glioma at age < 25 years

2 points

·    Any other malignancy at age < 18 years

1 point

C4CMMRD scoring points assigned to additional features in the patient (optional):

·    Clinical sign of NF1c and/or ≥ 4 hyperpigmented and/or hypopigmented skin alterations with diameter > 10 mm

2 points

·    2 or 3 hyperpigmented and/or hypopigmented skin alterations with diameter > 10 mm (do not count if 2 points are already given for clinical sign of NF1 and/or ≥ 4 hyperpigmented and/or hypopigmented skin alterations with diameter > 10 mm)

1 point

·    Multiple pilomatrixomas

2 points

·    One pilomatrixoma

1 point

·    Agenesis of the corpus callosum

1 point

·    Non–therapy-induced cavernoma

1 point

·    Multiple developmental venous anomalies (also known as cerebral venous angiomas) in separate regions of the brain

2 points

·    Paediatric systemic lupus erythematosus

1 point

·    Deficiency/reduced levels of IgG2/4 and/or IgA

1 point

C4CMMRD scoring points assigned to additional features in the family (optional):

·    Consanguineous parents

1 point

·    Diagnosis of LS in a first-degree or second-degree relative

2 points

·    Carcinoma from LS spectrumb before the age of 60 years in a first-degree, second-degree, and/or third-degree relative

1 point

·    A sibling with a (pre)malignancy assigned 2 or 3 C4CMMRD scoring points

2 points

·    A sibling with any type of childhood malignancy

1 point

Total score: CMMRD testing is indicated in a patient with cancer reaching ≥ 3 points

LS, Lynch syndrome; NF1, neurofibromatosis type 1.

aOriginal C4CMMRD criteria: Wimmer et al. {24737826}. bColorectal, endometrial, small bowel, urothelial, gastric, ovarian, and biliary tract cancer. cClinical sign in the patient used for the diagnosis of NF1 according to Legius et al. {34012067}.

diagnosis: MSH6-proficient crypts in MSH6 constitutional mismatch repair deficiency syndrome (CMMRD)
legend: MSH6 immunohistochemistry showing mismatch repair–proficient (MMRp)-crypt foci in a patient with MSH6 CMMRD who carried a germline MSH6 pathogenic variant (c.3261dupC) in trans with an MSH6 likely pathogenic variant (c.3724_3726del). A–D Monocryptic (A; scale bar: 50 µm), dicryptic (B; scale bar: 50 µm), tricryptic (C; scale bar: 50 µm), and polycryptic (D; scale bar: 100 µm) MSH6p foci. In the background, most crypts and stromal cells show complete loss of staining while some crypt cells show weak staining. E A group of adenomatous glands showing the presence of MSH6 staining with strong intensity while the background adenoma and non-adenomatous tissue all show loss of staining (scale bar: 500 µm). The staining for MLH1, MSH2, MSH3, and PMS2 was retained in all samples (not shown).
copyright: reproduced from: Shia J, Sanchez-Vega F, Cho S, et al. MSH6-proficient crypt foci in MSH6 constitutional mismatch repair deficiency: reversion of a frameshifted coding microsatellite to its wild-type sequence. Case Reports Fam Cancer. 2024 Nov;23(4):569-577. PMID: 39387980.
